# Geometry and Surface Priors

Also called: Geometric Constraints, Surface Regularization, Depth Priors

## Overview
Geometry and Surface Priors address the inherent lack of explicit geometric boundaries in standard 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS), where "floating" ellipsoids obscure the true surface topology [S1]. By enforcing positional and normal consistency with continuous geometric priors (such as SDFs, depth maps, or explicit meshes), these methods enable the extraction of watertight meshes and accurate material decomposition [S1]. They are distinguished from sibling methods like [NeuSG](9172-neusg.md) or [GSDF](9205-gsdf.md) by their specific approach to aligning discrete Gaussian parameters with external geometric constraints, ranging from post-hoc regularization [SuGaR](9191-sugar.md) to physically-based inverse rendering [Geo-Splatting](9201-geo-splatting.md).

## Shared principles
All methods in this family share the goal of aligning the discrete Gaussian representation with a continuous geometric prior. The core mechanism involves adding geometric loss terms to the standard photometric rendering loss $\mathcal{L}_{rgb}$. These losses typically enforce two properties:
1.  **Positional Consistency:** Gaussian centers $\mathbf{c}_i$ are encouraged to lie on the zero-level set of a distance function (SDF or UDF) or align with metric depth estimates.
2.  **Normal Consistency:** The orientation of the Gaussians (derived from their covariance matrix or rotation quaternion) is aligned with the surface normal estimated from the geometric prior.

The total loss function generally takes the form:
$$ \mathcal{L}_{total} = \mathcal{L}_{rgb} + \lambda_{geo} \mathcal{L}_{geo} + \lambda_{norm} \mathcal{L}_{norm} $$
where $\mathcal{L}_{geo}$ is the geometric consistency loss and $\mathcal{L}_{norm}$ is the normal consistency loss [S1]. The weights $\lambda_{geo}$ and $\lambda_{norm}$ are hyperparameters that balance photometric fidelity against geometric accuracy [S1].

## Subtopics

### [NeuSG](9172-neusg.md)
Integrates the NeuS implicit surface reconstruction framework into 3DGS to transfer explicit surface properties to discrete Gaussian primitives, solving the problem of "floating ellipsoids" by enforcing geometric consistency via a coupled SDF.

### [Monocular Depth Scale Alignment](9183-monocular-depth-scale-alignment.md)
A post-optimization step that resolves the up-to-scale ambiguity in multi-view reconstruction by aligning the metric scale of optimized 3D Gaussians with metric-scale monocular depth estimates, optimizing only a global scale factor.

### [Sparse-view 3D Gaussian Splatting with Depth Priors](9185-sparse-view-3d-gaussian-splatting-with-depth-priors.md)
Addresses geometric ambiguity in sparse-view inputs by explicitly integrating depth priors from pre-trained 2D monocular depth estimation networks to supervise the Gaussian distribution, rather than relying solely on implicit neural fields.

### [GSDF](9205-gsdf.md)
Aligns the discrete 3D Gaussian representation with a continuous Signed Distance Function (SDF) prior, encouraging Gaussian centers to lie on the zero-level set and normals to align with the SDF gradient.

### [Surface and Geometry Alignment](9267-surface-and-geometry-alignment.md)
A broad category of methods that enforce positional and normal consistency with continuous geometric priors to enable watertight mesh extraction, distinguished by their specific alignment strategies.

### GaussianPro
A method that considers neighboring views' normal direction consistency to produce better reconstruction results. It introduces a progressive propagation strategy for updating Gaussians, considering normal consistency between neighboring views, and adds plane constraints to guide the growth of 3D Gaussian Splatting [S1].

### 3DGSR
A method that encourages consistency between Signed Distance Function (SDF) and 3DGS to enhance geometry reconstruction quality [S1].

### Gaussian Splatting Surface Refinement
Uses pretrained volume rendering priors (UDF) to push Gaussians toward true surfaces by optimizing along the direction of increasing rendering weights, avoiding off-surface drift and discreteness. It is a post-training refinement strategy effective for open and thin structures, integrating the prior into existing variants without modifying inference-time resource costs [S2].

## Background
The standard 3D Gaussian Splatting representation, while efficient for novel view synthesis, produces a collection of discrete ellipsoids that do not inherently define a coherent surface [S1]. This "floating" nature makes it difficult to extract watertight meshes or perform geometry-aware tasks. To mitigate this, researchers have integrated geometric priors into the training loop. Early approaches like [NeuSG](9172-neusg.md) coupled 3DGS with implicit neural fields (NeuS) to enforce SDF consistency [S1]. Other methods, such as [GSDF](9205-gsdf.md) and [3DGSR](9267-surface-and-geometry-alignment.md#3dgshr), explicitly encourage consistency between the Gaussian distribution and a neural SDF field [S1]. For sparse-view scenarios, methods like [Sparse-view 3D Gaussian Splatting with Depth Priors](9185-sparse-view-3d-gaussian-splatting-with-depth-priors.md) leverage monocular depth estimators to provide additional geometric constraints [S1]. Post-optimization techniques like [Monocular Depth Scale Alignment](9183-monocular-depth-scale-alignment.md) address scale ambiguities that persist even after geometric regularization [S1]. More recent work, such as [Gaussian Splatting Surface Refinement](9267-surface-and-geometry-alignment.md#gaussian-splatting-surface-refinement), utilizes pretrained volume rendering priors to refine Gaussians toward true surfaces, particularly for thin and open structures where standard methods degrade [S2].
